settings.title: Settings
settings.lead: Household preferences, connected devices and maintenance.
settings.templatesLead: Add reusable messages, one per line.
settings.updateLead: Upload {0}. Clients compare its hash to their own and update if they differ — online ones now, offline ones when they reconnect. The previous build is kept as {1} on each PC for rollback.
settings.updateNote: The version is read out of the exe, so there is nothing to type. Builds from {0} are rejected — cut a release with {1} first. Re-uploading an older release is a rollback.
settings.backgroundsLead: Shown behind the block screen on every PC. Two pictures, because "you have used your hour" at four in the afternoon and "it is night" at half past nine are different messages, and the picture is the only part of that screen that says so without words.
settings.backgroundsNote: JPEG or PNG, up to 8 MB. Not WebP and not an iPhone HEIC — the PCs cannot draw those. A PC picks a new image up straight away if it is online, and on its next connection otherwise; any PC with its own image on its page keeps that one.
settings.versionsNone: No clients have reported a version yet.
settings.sessionsLead: Sessions are signed rather than stored, so they cannot be cancelled one at a time. Changing your password leaves other devices signed in — this is the button that does not.
settings.logoutAllConfirm: Sign out every device, including this one? Paired PCs are unaffected.
settings.sessionsNote: This rotates the Server Key. It signs admin sessions and nothing else — Clients, their tokens and the Admin Code are untouched.
settings.languageLead: The language of these pages. Each PC has its own, chosen on the PC itself from its tray menu — changing this does not change what a kid sees.
settings.aboutDevBuild: This tree is not the release it claims to be — it is past its tag, or has uncommitted changes. Cut a release with {0} to make the version mean one tree again.
settings.aboutProtocol: Wire protocol {0}. The server does not update itself ({1}) — a stale server blocks nobody, because PCs enforce from their own state. To update: {2}, then restart.
ok.passwordChanged: Password changed. Other devices stay signed in — use "Log out all devices" if that is not what you want.
err.tickToSkip: Tick the box to continue without an authenticator app.
err.codeNotAccepted: That code was not accepted. Check your phone's clock is set automatically — a phone running a few minutes off produces codes this server will reject.
ok.adminCodeUnproven: Admin Code is now in use — but nobody has proved they can produce a code from it.
coupons.title: Time Coupons
coupons.lead: Pre-made time codes you can print or send. The kid spends one whenever they choose — it adds its minutes to that day, and downtime still wins.
coupons.deleteConfirm: Delete the selected coupons? A printed copy stops working immediately.
err.couponBadInput: Those coupon details were not accepted. Check the amount, the count and the date.
client.backgroundsNote: What this PC shows behind its block screen. With nothing set here it uses the household images from Settings; each of the two is inherited on its own, so you can override one and keep the other.
client.noDowntimeHint: No downtime? Set start and end to the same time (e.g. 00:00 / 00:00).
client.lockedNote: Blocked by you until you unlock (or midnight).
client.endTodayConfirm: End today's time now? A new code can still give time back.
client.disableConfirm: Disable this PC? It stops enforcing until you enable it again here.
client.disabledNote: Currently disabled — no limits are enforced.
client.disableNote: Stops all enforcement; re-enable any time from here.
client.revokeConfirm: Revoke this client's token? It keeps enforcing standalone.
client.deleteConfirm: Delete this client and ALL its history?
header.protocolMismatch: This client speaks protocol {0}, this server speaks {1}. Both keep working; some newer messages may be ignored by one side.
req.noneOpen: No one is waiting on you.
requests.lead: Live asks first; the history below keeps the pattern visible.
req.noneOpenNote: A Request appears here when a kid asks for more time from the tray or the block screen. It stops being answerable an hour later, or at midnight.
req.offlineTitle: Answer anyway — the verdict waits up to 30 minutes for the PC to come back
req.declineNote: Declining starts a 15-minute quiet period before they can ask again.
req.withdrawn: withdrawn — an extra time code was used instead
bg.blockedBlurb: Shown when the day's time is used up — and when you lock a PC or end its day.
bg.downtimeBlurb: Shown during the nightly downtime window.
bg.none: No image — the block screen is plain.

codes.title: Admin Code
codes.lead: Immediate ways to grant time, plus the household credentials used when the server cannot help.
codes.unprovenTitle: Nobody has proved this Admin Code is in an authenticator app.
codes.unprovenBody: If this server is unreachable, you will not be able to stop Digital Aid on a PC or pair a new one.
codes.unprovenNote: Scan it into your phone from the code below, then type back what it shows. If you no longer have the secret, regenerate below and confirm the new one.
codes.offlineStrip: Server unreachable — codes are being computed on this device.
codes.noCrypto: This page is open over an insecure connection, so the browser will not let it compute or copy codes. Open it over HTTPS.
codes.extraNote: This is the one you read out. Pick how long, then read the whole number out — every digit, including the minutes on the end. Your choice is remembered on this device.
codes.extraOnceNote: One code can only be redeemed once on a PC — if you need to give more time again, read out the next one rather than repeating this.
codes.adminWarnBody: Anyone who has these six digits can {0} on a PC, or pair that PC to a different server. Don't read it out.
codes.adminNote: The same code your authenticator app shows. Use it to set up a new PC, or to turn the app off on one yourself. It never gives time.
codes.trustOffLead: Codes are being fetched from the server, so this tab stops working if the server is unreachable — which tends to happen at exactly the moment a PC is blocked and you need a code.
codes.trustOffNote: Trusting this device stores both household secrets in this browser so codes are worked out here instead — extra-time codes can only come from here or from the server. Do it on your own phone, not a shared one; it cannot be undone remotely, only by regenerating below.
codes.trustedOn: This device is trusted — codes are computed here and keep working offline.
codes.untrust: Forget the secrets on this device
codes.whyTitle: Why your authenticator can't give time
codes.whyBody1: An extra-time code is not built from the 6-digit code any more. It comes off a second household secret that only this server and your trusted devices hold, so a code you read out reveals nothing about the one that stops the app — you can hand out extra time all week without ever giving away the way out of the block screen.
codes.whyBody2: It also means there is nothing to work out by hand. If you want codes with the server down, trust the device above; that is what the offline path is for.
codes.whyNote: Your authenticator app still matters — it pairs a PC and it stops one, which is the emergency you actually need a phone for. Every use is recorded on the PC's page with the minutes actually given.
codes.regenBody: Both household secrets are replaced together — the one your authenticator holds and the one behind extra-time codes. Online PCs pick the new pair up immediately, offline ones on their next connection. Any trusted device keeps a copy of the old pair, which stops working the moment you do this.
codes.regenConfirm: Regenerate both household secrets? Your authenticator entry must be replaced, and trusted devices must be trusted again.
codes.couponsLead: Pre-made time codes you can print and hand out — spent whenever the kid chooses, checked by the server.
prove.title: Add this to your phone
prove.leadRest: (or any TOTP app), then type the six digits it shows back to us. That is the only way to know the code exists somewhere other than this server.
prove.backupNote: Keep the text above somewhere safe as a backup. This is the {0}: it pairs a new PC and stops the app on one. It does not give time.
prove.warn: If this server is ever unreachable — and a blocked PC and a dead server tend to turn up together — your phone is the only thing that can still stop Digital Aid on a PC or pair a new one. A code that lives only in this database is a code nobody has.
prove.codeLabel: The six digits your app is showing now
prove.skipSummary: I can't scan this right now
prove.skipNote: Fine for a test server, or if you have thought about it. The code still becomes the one in force — it simply goes unproven, and the Codes page will keep saying so until someone confirms it.
prove.skipAck: I'm not putting this in an authenticator app. I understand that if this server is unreachable, I won't be able to stop Digital Aid on a PC or pair a new one.
prove.restartNote: If the scan went wrong, or you are not sure which entry in your app this is, throw this one away and start again.
prove.restartSubmit: Start over with a new code
prove.cancelNote: Your current Admin Code is still in force and the PCs have not been told anything. Backing out now leaves everything exactly as it was.
js.offlineTrusted: Server unreachable — codes are being computed on this device.
js.offlineUntrusted: Server unreachable, and this device is not trusted, so it cannot work out codes on its own. Your authenticator app can still stop or pair a PC — but nothing can give extra time until the server is back or you trust a device.
js.copyFailed: Could not copy — select it by hand
js.untrustConfirm: Forget the secrets on this device? Codes will need the server again.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.note: Alerts reach a phone that is in a pocket, which the count in the menu bar cannot. Every device you have turned them on for gets everything switched on here — there is no per-device choice, and no Approve or Decline button on a notification. Tapping one opens this app.
alerts.request: A kid asks for more time
alerts.requestNote: Also replaces itself with the answer once one of you has decided, so a question nobody is waiting on any more does not sit on the other phone.
alerts.startedNote: After ten quiet minutes, so a brief network drop is not mistaken for a PC being switched on. Not sent when this server itself was restarted, or when several PCs come back together — that is the network, not the household.
alerts.exhausted: A PC runs out of time
alerts.exhaustedNote: Only running out. Downtime arrives at the same minute every night by your own rule, and locking a PC yourself is something you already know about.
alerts.lockedNote: After the screen has been locked for ten minutes, so stopping for lunch does not send anything.
alerts.couponNote: Sent when a kid enters a Time Coupon.
alerts.grant: An Extra Time Code is used
alerts.grantNote: Sent when a kid enters an Extra Time Code.

download.lead: Install Digital Aid on a PC.
download.contents: A zip holding the client app and the install and uninstall scripts.
download.step1: If the installer says the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime is missing, let it install it — or install it yourself with {0}.
download.step2: Unzip everything into one folder and double-click {0}. Approve the Windows prompt for administrator rights.
download.step3: The app appears in the tray. Pair it from the tray menu with a current admin code — until then it enforces nothing.
download.blocked: If Windows says it protected your PC, the download was blocked as unrecognised: open the zip's Properties and tick Unblock before unzipping, then run {0} again.
download.noBuild: No client build is available on this server right now. Upload one from Settings after logging in.
